source.title: A Tale of Two Symmetries: Exploring the Loss Landscape of Equivariant Models

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper’s own toy experiments show that an equivariantly constrained student can converge to a spurious minimum and that relaxing the constraint can let it reach a global minimum. This refines the broad claim about training success but does not test any listed version’s specific setting or recipe.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes are toy teacher-student loss landscapes and training runs, not CIFAR benchmarks, width comparisons, depth or initialization sweeps, learning-rate stability tests, or batch-normalization comparisons. Rows below record the toy training and relaxation results; cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests optimization barriers caused by equivariance constraints and escape through constraint relaxation. It does not test any listed version: notably, it neither varies teacher/student width nor measures whether extra neurons reduce spurious-minimum convergence under standard initialization (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under stated conditions, hidden parameter symmetries induce critical points and additional minima in constrained models. Toy experiments demonstrate spurious minima and show that constraint relaxation can sometimes turn them into saddles, permitting convergence to a global minimum associated with a different hidden-layer group representation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses exact-loss gradient descent in a small equivariant teacher-student setup with selected parameter values; it does not reproduce the listed benchmark, depth, initialization, learning-rate, or normalization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The training outcome depends on the initial diagonal and off-diagonal weights; the boundary also changes shape with parameterization. The paper reports similar patterns across random teacher seeds, while noting exceptions and additional unexplained boundaries.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected initializations of a constrained two-layer ReLU student converge to a spurious minimum despite an achievable perfect solution. Parameter rescaling changes the boundary between convergence regions; removing equivariance constraints can permit escape to a global minimum with a different hidden-layer representation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Equivariance constraints can create optimization barriers in realizable teacher-student networks, and relaxing those constraints can sometimes permit escape without increasing width.

record.problems: Toy experiments use a limited setup; statistical uncertainty is not reported. Results are mainly shown in figures, and the paper notes some seed cases where minima are not apparent or outside the sweep range, plus unexplained boundaries in some runs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Seed-specific plots and activation/spherical-signal experiments are figure-only and do not provide separate text-described outcomes suitable for additional rows under the stated extraction rules.

untested.parts: Training classification error of large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious-minimum convergence frequency as teacher and student grow together under standard initialization, and its reduction from adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability trajectories, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: T6 applies relative to the six specified versions, despite the study's substantive optimization results. Appendix experiments do not supply the missing width, initialization-scheme, depth, stability-threshold, or normalization comparisons. States of cannot_determine reflect the lack of a matching claim version, not uncertainty about the reported toy outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, random initialization, corrupted or random labels, size comparisons, and early stopping or regularized recipes.
No teacher/student width sweep or comparison giving the student one or two more neurons than the teacher.
No depth sweep, plain versus residual shortcut comparison, ImageNet/CIFAR-10 experiment, or Fixup experiment.
No comparison of initialization schemes for signal/gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or very deep plain networks.
No learning-rate stability threshold or sharpness trajectory comparison.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: student network
rows.size_stated: 2-layer; hidden layer has one π0 rep and 3 trivial π0 reps
rows.operation_detail: Trained by gradient descent on the exact loss for 100 steps across initial diagonal and off-diagonal weights.

conditions.value: varied θ1 and θ2; remaining student weights equal teacher weights
diagonal and off-diagonal components parameterized directly

rows.value: Two regions: one converges to a global minimum and one does not; boundary is curved.
rows.note: Text describes the regions and boundary; no numeric loss values are stated.
rows.check: The two convergence regions are reported correctly, but they do not measure any listed version. The hidden-layer description repeats an apparent source typo: the experiment requires one π3 block plus three trivial π0 blocks, rather than four trivial blocks. Specify that only input-to-hidden weights are trainable and the output weights are fixed to ones.

rows.subject: student network
rows.size_stated: 2-layer; hidden layer has one π0 rep and 3 trivial π0 reps
rows.operation_detail: Trained by gradient descent on the exact loss for 100 steps after rescaling the diagonal parameter.

conditions.value: varied θ1 and θ2; remaining student weights equal teacher weights

rows.value: Two regions: one converges to a global minimum and one does not; boundary is a straight line corresponding to the hidden fixed point subspace.
rows.note: Text describes the regions and boundary; no numeric loss values are stated.
rows.check: The straight convergence boundary after rescaling is reported correctly, but parameterization sensitivity does not test V4's activation-matched initialization claim. Correct the apparent hidden-layer typo to one π3 block plus three trivial π0 blocks; output weights are fixed to ones.

rows.subject: equivariant student network, then unconstrained network initialized at its bad minimum
rows.operation_detail: Trained the constrained student to its bad minimum, then removed equivariance constraints and continued training until convergence.
rows.baseline: Constrained student reaches a bad minimum.
rows.value: Relaxed network reaches a global minimum; final weights are permuted relative to teacher weights and correspond to a different hidden-layer group representation.
rows.note: Authors describe the constrained and relaxed outcomes in text; no numerical loss values are stated.
rows.check: Escape to a global minimum after removing equivariance constraints is explicitly reported. This changes the allowed parameter space without adding neurons, so it does not measure V2's extra-width effect or another listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
